title: Hotel Eden vs Hotel de Russie: Quiet Street or Courtyard? (2026) | Suites With Keith
description: Hotel Eden vs Hotel de Russie, compared by a travel advisor who stayed at the Eden and visited the de Russie in October 2026: quiet, courtyard, rooms, suites, spa, price, and who each one suits.

hero.alt: Hotel de Russie’s large courtyard, with white umbrellas over tables and salmon-pink walls

sub: Two Rome hotels I loved, and both are calm in the middle of the city. One finds it on a quiet street above the Spanish Steps; the other finds it in a big courtyard off a busy one. Here is how I would choose.
stamp: Stayed at the Eden · Visited the de Russie · October 2026

band.h2: Do you want your calm on the street outside, or behind the walls?
paras: Hotel Eden sits on a quiet residential street just above the Spanish Steps. You are close to everything, and you still come home to calm. It is my top overall pick in Rome, and usually a little cheaper than the de Russie.

The Hotel de Russie is on a busy street between Piazza del Popolo and the Spanish Steps. Walk in, though, and the large courtyard feels like an escape from the city. It also has a spa with an indoor pool, which is rare in the centro storico.
If you want quiet from the moment you step outside, pick the Eden. If a courtyard and a pool matter more to you than a quiet street, pick the de Russie. I loved them both.

guide.alt: The bar in Hotel de Russie’s courtyard, with arched blue shelves of bottles and a mosaic-fronted marble counter
paras: The courtyard is really the star of the Hotel de Russie. It is beautiful and large, it is where everyone gathers, and there is a bar in it with arched blue shelves of bottles. Step back out the front, though, and you are in the crowds.
At Hotel Eden, the calm starts at the front door. The street itself is calm, residential and just above the Steps, while its big-name competitors open onto the crowds.

guide.alt: A white marble Hotel Eden bathroom with a deep soaking tub and brass fixtures
paras: The rooms at Hotel Eden are modern and traditional at once, bright and beautifully decorated, with incredible views over the rooftops and marble bathrooms with deep soaking tubs and double vanities.

The Hotel de Russie rooms have been renovated, and they have the cutest ceilings, each one either lemon or orange themed. Bathrooms are in veined marble, some with a mosaic of birds set into the shower.

guide.alt: A Hotel de Russie suite terrace looking over Piazza del Popolo’s obelisk to the hills
paras: At the Hotel de Russie, I saw a stunning suite with fantastic views, with a terrace looking over the obelisk in Piazza del Popolo to the hills. Ask me and I will tell you which one.
At Hotel Eden, the top suites are spacious on their own and can be combined into larger configurations for families or two couples traveling together. I will map out what is possible.

guide.alt: Hotel Eden’s glass-roofed rooftop restaurant at golden hour, with views over Rome’s rooftops
paras: The restaurant upstairs at Hotel Eden was fantastic, and the view across the domes is the one I send couples to on their first evening. The Eden is usually priced slightly below the de Russie, for a stay I would rank above it.
The Hotel de Russie spa has an indoor pool, a real draw after a day on foot. The dining rooms have hand-painted walls of palms and lemon trees, and the courtyard is the place for a drink.

faq.q: Which is better, Hotel Eden or Hotel de Russie?
faq.a: For me, Hotel Eden: it is my top overall pick in Rome, with a quiet street and usually a slightly lower rate. I loved the Hotel de Russie too, and it is the one to pick if the courtyard and an indoor pool appeal.
Hotel Eden, on a calm residential street. The street out front of the Hotel de Russie is busy, but the courtyard inside feels like an escape from the city.
The Hotel de Russie has a nice spa with an indoor pool, which is rare in the centro storico.
Usually Hotel Eden, slightly below the de Russie. I can quote them side by side for your dates.

faq.q: Which room should I book at each?
faq.a: At Hotel Eden, ask about the top suites, which can be connected. At the Hotel de Russie, the suite with the fantastic views I saw; I will tell you which one.

faq.q: Is the de Russie better than its sister, the de la Ville?
faq.a: For me, yes. Both are Rocco Forte hotels a few minutes apart, and the de Russie’s courtyard, renovated rooms and indoor pool made it the stronger stay over the Hotel de la Ville.
